conceptBreakdown.title: 1. Alcohol Classifications & Physical Trends

summaryBox.title: Alcohol Taxonomy & Boiling Point
summaryBox.takeaway: Boiling points: 1° > 2° > 3° due to larger surface area in unbranched chains. Extensive intermolecular H-bonding elevates alcohol boiling points above ethers and alkanes.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Alcohols contain one or more hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) groups attached to $sp^3$-hybridized aliphatic carbon atoms, following the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}\text{OH}$.

**Physical Properties & Hydrogen Bonding:**
1. **Boiling Point Trends**: Alcohols possess significantly higher boiling points than corresponding alkanes, haloalkanes, or ethers of comparable molecular weight due to extensive Intermolecular Hydrogen Bonding.
   - *Branching Effect*: For isomeric alcohols, boiling point decreases with increasing chain branching ($\mathbf{1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ}$) because spherical branching reduces surface area and weakens van der Waals dispersion forces.
2. **Water Solubility**: Lower alcohols ($\text{MeOH, EtOH, PrOH}$) are miscible with water in all proportions via hydrogen bonding with $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Solubility decreases as the hydrophobic alkyl chain ($\text{R}-$) expands.

conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Synthetic Hydration Pathways from Alkenes
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ALKENE HYDRATION PATHWAYS
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
ACID-CATALYZED HYDRATION         OXYMERCURATION-DEMERCURATION     HYDROBORATION-OXIDATION
($\text{H}^+ / \text{H}_2\text{O}$) ($\text{OMDM}$)                  ($\text{HBO}$)
├── Markovnikov addition        ├── **Markovnikov addition**      ├── **Anti-Markovnikov addition**
├── **Carbocation Intermediate**   ├── Cyclic mercurinium ion        ├── **Syn-addition** of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
└── **PRONE TO REARRANGEMENTS**  └── **NO REARRANGEMENTS**        └── $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{OH}^-$
conceptBreakdown.content:
Three distinct hydration pathways synthesize alcohols from alkenes:
- **Acid-Catalyzed Hydration**: Markovnikov addition proceeding via carbocation intermediate; prone to 1,2-hydride/methyl shifts.
- **Oxymercuration-Demercuration (OMDM)**: Markovnikov addition via cyclic mercurinium ion with NO carbocation rearrangement.
- **Hydroboration-Oxidation (HBO)**: Anti-Markovnikov syn-addition of water across the double bond without rearrangement.

quickRevision: OMDM: Markovnikov + NO rearrangements (cyclic mercurinium ion).
HBO: Anti-Markovnikov + Syn-addition of H₂O (BH₃·THF, then alkaline H₂O₂).
